read.thesis: Bank read: no change to guidance despite Middle East conflict; ECL and IFRS 9 overlay risk flagged, with 14–14.5% CET1 range and buybacks paused through Q2 2026 unchanged. Supply-side metrics not applicable to a bank.

triggers.label: IFRS 9 reserve build risk if conflict persists
triggers.quote: if the stress continues for longer, we do have a trillion-dollar balance sheet. There would inevitably be some further stress on the balance sheet, and that would impact the ECL guidance.

triggers.label: ECL guidance unchanged for 2026
triggers.quote: As of now, based on everything we know we have not changed our ECL guidance for the year.

guidance.quote: In terms of banking NII – giving guidance just for this year - based upon the trajectory, we look at it as a low single digit, 1%, sort of growth level.
so mid-to-low single digits – that’s the trajectory we’ve seen and we are looking at.
our guidance is at least 17% ROTE, the operative words there are ‘at least’
it is a range of 14% to 14.5% - on which all the guidance and the targets are based.

prior_guidance_check.quote: as at 9 October, when we said a three-quarter- pause, that really is fourth quarter last year, first quarter this year, second quarter this year as well.

red_flags.label: Private credit second/third-order risk
red_flags.quote: some of the private credit exposures which are highly leveraged because of liquidity constraints may come under further pressure

red_flags.label: Fraud risk and double pledging concerns
red_flags.quote: If you ask me, ‘will there be more issues in this space?’ the answer is yes.

evasions.quote: nothing changes for that, irrespective of what’s happened the last five days
